risk: Liquidity is managed on forecasts that are consistently wrong, so the organisation borrows expensively or is caught short.
audit_objective: Assess whether cash forecasting is accurate enough to support liquidity decisions.
what_to_review: Forecast methodology, horizon and granularity
Accuracy of prior forecasts against actual outcomes
Inclusion of committed capital, tax and debt service outflows
Headroom against facilities and covenant limits
Escalation when forecast headroom falls below threshold
procedures: Compare prior forecasts to actual cash outcomes and quantify the error by horizon.
Test whether known commitments were included in forecasts or omitted.
Test facility headroom at several dates and whether escalation occurred where policy required.
Assess whether business units feed the forecast on a consistent basis.
red_flags: Forecast error consistently in one direction
Committed outflows appearing only when they hit
Headroom breaches noticed after the fact
Forecast prepared by one person with no challenge
plain: Running out of cash kills otherwise profitable businesses. The forecast is what stops that happening.

risk: A covenant is breached, or a facility lapses, because compliance is monitored manually and only at reporting dates.
audit_objective: Confirm borrowing arrangements are tracked and covenant compliance is monitored continuously.
what_to_review: Inventory of facilities, maturities and renewal timelines
Covenant definitions and how they are calculated
Frequency of covenant monitoring versus testing dates
Headroom trend and forecast covenant compliance
Reporting obligations to lenders and their timeliness
procedures: Recompute covenants from the lender definitions rather than from management's summary; definitions often differ from statutory measures.
Test covenant headroom at each test date and on a forecast basis.
Test that lender reporting obligations were met within the required timeframe.
Review maturity profile and refinancing plans for concentration risk.
red_flags: Covenants calculated using management-adjusted figures
Headroom thin and narrowing without escalation
Lender reporting submitted late
Facilities maturing within twelve months with no refinancing plan
plain: Loan agreements contain promises. Break one and the lender can demand its money back immediately.

subprocess: Foreign Exchange and Interest Rate Risk
risk: Exposures are hedged on incomplete data or not at all, so earnings swing on market movements the organisation never chose to take.
audit_objective: Assess whether market risk exposures are identified, measured and managed within policy.
what_to_review: Completeness of exposure identification from the business
Hedging policy, ratios and permitted instruments
Effectiveness of hedges and any hedge accounting applied
Speculative positions and policy breaches
Counterparty exposure and credit limits
procedures: Reconcile hedged exposures to underlying business exposures and quantify unhedged or over-hedged positions.
Test compliance with the hedging policy ratio at several dates.
Test that instruments used are on the permitted list and that no speculative positions exist.
Test hedge effectiveness documentation where hedge accounting is applied.
red_flags: Over-hedging, which is speculation by another name
Exposures identified only from the ledger, missing forecast transactions
Instruments used outside the approved list
Effectiveness testing prepared retrospectively
plain: Currency and interest rate moves can swing profit even when the business is performing exactly as planned.

risk: Surplus cash is placed with counterparties or in instruments outside policy, risking capital for marginal yield.
audit_objective: Confirm investments comply with policy on instrument, counterparty and tenor.
what_to_review: Approved instrument and counterparty lists with credit limits
Concentration by counterparty and rating
Tenor and liquidity of investments against cash needs
Valuation and income recognition
Authorisation of placements and rollovers
procedures: Test each investment held against the approved instrument and counterparty list and applicable limits.
Analyse concentration by counterparty and rating band against policy.
Test authorisation for placements and rollovers, including who can instruct the bank.
Agree valuations and accrued income to independent confirmations.
red_flags: Yield chasing into unapproved instruments
Concentration with one counterparty above limit
Rollovers executed without fresh authorisation
Valuations sourced from the counterparty alone
plain: Chasing slightly better returns with spare cash is how companies lose money they were not trying to risk.

risk: Funds move between group entities without documentation, creating tax exposure, regulatory breach and balances nobody can reconcile.
audit_objective: Confirm intragroup funding is documented, priced and permitted in each jurisdiction.
what_to_review: Loan agreements and documentation for intragroup funding
Interest pricing and transfer pricing compliance
Cash pooling arrangements and participant agreements
Regulatory restrictions on cross-border movement and repatriation
Reconciliation of intercompany balances
procedures: Test that intragroup funding has executed agreements and that interest is charged and paid per those terms.
Test transfer pricing documentation supporting intragroup interest rates.
Reconcile pooling balances between participants and the header account.
Test compliance with local restrictions on capital movement for a sample of jurisdictions.
red_flags: Funding advanced with no agreement
Interest accrued but never settled
Pool balances unreconciled between entities
Repatriation executed without checking local rules
plain: Money moved between group companies without proper agreements creates tax and legal problems later.

subprocess: Guarantees, Letters of Credit and Off-Balance Sheet Commitments
risk: Guarantees and contingent commitments are given and forgotten, so the organisation carries obligations that appear nowhere in its reporting.
audit_objective: Confirm contingent obligations are authorised, recorded, monitored and disclosed.
what_to_review: Register of guarantees, letters of credit, bonds and indemnities
Authorisation and who may commit the organisation
Expiry monitoring and release of expired instruments
Fees paid on unused or expired facilities
Disclosure of contingent liabilities
procedures: Obtain confirmations from banks of all instruments outstanding and reconcile to the internal register.
Test authorisation for instruments issued in the period.
Identify expired instruments still incurring fees and test whether release was pursued.
Reconcile the register to contingent liability disclosure.
red_flags: Bank confirmations revealing instruments not on the register
Guarantees issued by subsidiaries without group approval
Fees paid on instruments no longer needed
Contingent liabilities disclosed only in round terms
plain: Guarantees are promises to pay if someone else does not. They are easy to give and easy to forget.

subprocess: Treasury System Access and Dealing Controls
risk: A single treasury user can create, confirm and settle a deal, allowing funds to be moved with no independent check.
audit_objective: Confirm dealing, confirmation and settlement are segregated and that treasury system access reflects that.
what_to_review: Segregation between front, middle and back office
System roles and conflicting access combinations
Independent confirmation of deals with counterparties
Standing settlement instructions and their amendment
Dealer mandates, limits and recorded lines
procedures: Map treasury system roles against a segregation matrix and test for users able to deal and settle.
Test independent confirmation of a sample of deals directly with counterparties.
Test amendments to standing settlement instructions for independent verification.
Test dealer authority against mandates for a sample of transactions.
red_flags: Dealers able to amend settlement instructions
Confirmations returned to the dealer rather than the back office
Standing instructions changed without verification
Deals executed outside recorded lines
evidence: Treasury system user and role listings
plain: If the same person can do a deal and settle it, money can move with no independent check at all.

subprocess: Bank Account Governance and Fee Analysis
risk: Bank accounts exist outside treasury's knowledge and banking fees are paid without review, wasting money and creating fraud exposure.
audit_objective: Confirm the organisation knows every bank account it holds and pays only the fees it agreed.
what_to_review: Completeness of the bank account inventory
Account opening and closing authority
Dormant accounts and their closure
Bank fee schedules versus fees charged
Bank service quality and rationalisation opportunities
procedures: Obtain confirmations directly from all banking relationships and reconcile to the internal account inventory.
Test account opening and closing authorisation for the period.
Identify dormant accounts and test why they remain open.
Recompute a sample of bank charges against the agreed fee schedule.
red_flags: Accounts confirmed by banks that treasury did not know about
Accounts opened by local management
Dormant accounts retained "just in case"
Fees charged above the agreed tariff
plain: Companies routinely have bank accounts nobody at head office knows about.
